blocks.text: 抛开公司丑闻不谈（这类事已经不少了），这件事将对 AI 热潮产生重大影响。

blocks.text: 毫无疑问，英伟达一直是这轮热潮的关键支点。截至 2026 年的五年间，该公司售出近 1400 万颗旗舰 AI 芯片，占据 85% 的市场份额。公司还为一批新兴 AI 基础设施企业（即所谓“新云”）提供财务担保，帮助它们启动业务。它也是 AI 公司的重要风险投资方，过去一年仅在欧洲就投入近 100 亿美元，是当地最大的投资者。

blocks.text: 这些数字还不足以体现黄仁勋本人的重要性。这不像失去史蒂夫·乔布斯的苹果。2011 年乔布斯卸任 CEO、不久后离世时，留下了一位充分了解情况的继任者和一支客户与市场都熟悉的管理团队。而如果说英伟达是 AI 热潮的关键支点，那么黄仁勋就是英伟达的关键支点。

blocks.text: 我认为他是最了解 AI 动向的人，原因很简单：一切都跑在他的芯片上。他倡导开源模型，包括如今让人有些不安的中国模型，并推动对中国采取更通融的态度。

blocks.text: 我在伦敦见过他几次。有一次，他和时任首相基尔·斯塔默一起从街上走来，登上舞台。他精力充沛，动辄砸出数十亿美元。他会点名一家初创公司，然后说“我投你 5 亿美元”之类的数字。他还把我们那份《AI 经济现状》报告的打印件还给我，封面用金色马克笔签了名，说这份现在更值钱了。今天之后可能更值钱。

blocks.text: 这个关键支点看来并非由坚固的钢铁铸成，倒更像一块用旧的皮革。依赖它的整个生态，还能继续在路上跑吗？

blocks.text: Company scandal aside, and there has been a lot, it’ll have a big impact on the AI boom.

inlines.text: Company scandal aside, and there has been a lot, it’ll have a big impact on the AI boom.

blocks.text: Nvidia has been, without doubt, the linchpin of that boom. In the five years to 2026, the firm sold nearly 14 million flagship AI chips. They account for 85% of the market. The company has provided financial guarantees to the constellation of upstart AI infrastructure companies, the so-called neoclouds, so they can get their business moving. It has been a substantial venture capital backer of AI companies, with nearly $10 billion across Europe in the last year – the biggest investor there.

blocks.text: The numbers don’t do justice to how important Jensen himself has been. This isn’t like Apple without Steve Jobs. When Steve Jobs relinquished the CEO role in 2011, shortly before he passed away, he left a well-briefed successor and a management team known to customers and the market alike. And if Nvidia has been the linchpin of the AI boom, Jensen has been the linchpin of Nvidia.

blocks.text: I thought of him as the person with the best visibility into what was going on in AI, simply because everything ran on his chips. He advocated open-source models, including, uncomfortably now, Chinese ones. And pushed for a more accommodating approach to China.

blocks.text: I’ve seen him in London a couple of times. Once, he arrived on stage from down the street with then-Prime Minister Keir Starmer in tow. He brings energy and hands out billions of dollars. Calling out a startup’s name, followed by “I’m backing you with $500m” or whatever the number was. He returned a printout of our State of the AI Economy report, his signature across the front in gold marker, telling me it would be worth more now. Maybe even more after today.
